first_pass.description: The ninety-second read, recorded before the methodology was opened.

divergence.description: Where the first pass disagreed with brief.core_claim; empty when it matched.

why.description: Anchored in a section, figure, or table.

attack.description: Written as the reviewer would write it.

evidence.description: The section, figure, or table it points at.

would_change_mind.description: What evidence or edit satisfies the attack; an unsatisfiable review cannot be acted on.

evidence_ready.description: False when the unit needs evidence that does not exist yet.

storyline_notes.description: Where the arc worked and where the paper lost the reader, paragraph by paragraph. The note only a reader can give.

first_pass.believed_claim: A single operator grammar plus its harness reaches hand-tuned performance without per-operator code.
first_pass.believed_headline: 1.58x over the released baseline on sparse GEMM.
first_pass.check_first: Whether the 1.58x baseline was tuned for the same shapes.
first_pass.divergence: The abstract promises dense and sparse; the introduction's result sentence mentions only sparse, so a reviewer reads the dense claim as unsupported.

scores.why: The grammar is a genuine delta over per-operator templates, but §2.3 does not cite the closest recent template DSL, so the reviewer cannot locate the boundary.
Table 3's baseline uses the shapes from the earlier paper; Fig. 5 shows spread with two points per operator.
§3.2 reads cleanly and the figure captions state claims rather than titles.

issues.attack: The evaluation compares against a baseline tuned for a different shape set, so the reported gap is not attributable to the design.
issues.fix: Re-run the baseline at the evaluated shapes, or move the comparison to an appendix and restate §5.2's claim.
issues.would_change_mind: A same-shape baseline row with the tuning budget stated.

issues.attack: The dense-GEMM claim in the abstract is never evaluated; §5 covers sparse only.
issues.fix: Either add the dense evaluation or narrow the abstract to sparse GEMM.
issues.would_change_mind: Two dense shapes in Fig. 5, or an abstract that claims sparse only.

next_round_target.reason: It carries the headline comparison the reviewer attacked first, and its current baseline is not shape-matched.

example.storyline_notes: §1's tension-to-insight move works in three paragraphs, matching the reference spec. §3.2 lost me at ¶4, where the check taxonomy arrives before the reader knows why any check is needed — the opener has no bridge from §3.1's layout requirement. §5.1 states the result before defining the metric.
